title: AI-Assisted Scouting: Where Algorithms Could Help Royal Challengers Bengaluru Recruit
dek: Where could algorithms genuinely help Royal Challengers Bengaluru recruit? A small, honest model shows how much of next season's batting can be predicted, and how much cannot.
excerpt: Trained on IPL seasons up to 2019 and tested on later ones, a four-feature model predicts next season's relative strike rate better than simple rules of thumb. Its errors are the real lesson for AI-assisted scouting.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

The model beats both rules of thumb, but most of the variation in next season's form remains unpredictable.

sections.heading: What an Algorithm Can Do
body: AI-assisted scouting promises to find patterns humans miss. The honest first question is how predictable player performance actually is.

CricField trained a small model on {{ev:ai-train}} batter-season pairs up to 2019, using four features of one season (relative strike rate, boundary rate, dot-ball rate and balls faced) to predict the next season's relative strike rate.

sections.heading: How It Did
body: On {{ev:ai-test}} pairs from 2020 onwards, the model's average error was {{ev:ai-model}} index points. Predicting the same as last season erred by {{ev:ai-pers}}, and predicting the league average by {{ev:ai-mean}}.

sections.heading: Where Algorithms Help
body: Even a modest edge helps when applied across hundreds of candidates: models are good at screening and at correcting for small samples, venue and era. They are weak at role fit, temperament and injury risk.

sections.heading: What This Model Is Not
body: It is deliberately simple and uses IPL data only. Richer inputs, such as ball-tracking, domestic cricket and other leagues, would improve it, at the cost of transparency.
Any production model should report its error against these baselines.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Use Models to Screen, People to Decide
body: Royal Challengers Bengaluru should use algorithms to screen and rank candidates and to flag small-sample traps, and leave final decisions to scouts who can judge role and character.
The model's error is the measure of how much human judgement is still needed.
